problem: Let X be connected and compact, dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial, and fix a smooth positive probability volume dV. All potentials are genuine canonical quasi-psh representatives, with pole values included. A smooth real (1,1) background theta is big if theta+dd^c rho>=epsilon h for a genuine potential rho, a Hermitian h and epsilon>0; it need not be closed. Ordinary order u preceq v means u<=v+C, and equivalence is mutual order. I(tu) uses |g|^2 exp(-tu), with no extra factor 2; ideal equivalence means equality at every real t>0. P_(theta,F)[u] is the usc supremum of theta-psh v<=F with v preceq u; P_(theta,F)[u]_I uses ideal-equivalent competitors. The zero-obstacle operations are P_theta[u] and P_theta[u]_I. An ordinary model is a normalized fixed point p=P_theta[p], and an ideal model also satisfies p=P_theta[p]_I. Extended products are non-pluripolar products with smooth-background corrections. Lower and upper singularity volumes are the infimum and supremum of extended mass over the entire fixed ordinary type, not the raw mass of one representative. BMP means finite supremum v_+(h) over all bounded h-psh potentials, and positive lower mass means the corresponding infimum v_-(h)>0; these are separate properties. Original S10 asks to relate Hermitian Perron interpolation and Legendre-dual test curves to geodesics of a complete metric on singularity classes, and to stationarity for a specified coherent action. On a strip S_I={z:Re z in I}, a subgeodesic has quasi-psh complexification U(x,z)=u_(Re z)(x) with pr_X*theta+dd^c U>=0. For two endpoints, their Perron segment is the usc supremum of such paths whose joint boundary upper limits are at most the endpoints, with genuine L1 endpoint attainment to be proved. Fixed ordinary-equivalent endpoints admit affine maximum barriers, so every slice has that same ordinary type; a metric projection must account for this. A test curve Gamma_tau consists of normalized ordinary models, pointwise concave and decreasing in tau, with usc supremum phi, cutoff c and minus-infinity extension for tau>c. Its forward transform is U_t=(sup_(tau<c)(Gamma_tau+t tau))^*, and the inverse is inf_(t>0)(U_t-t tau). Their Perron/Legendre correspondence already works without closedness. Known background: the raw L2 metric on smooth positive potentials is G_u(v,w)=integral v w (theta+dd^c u)^n, with action one half integral_0^1 G_(u_t)(dot u_t,dot u_t)dt. Its Euler equation has first-derivative torsion terms and a dd^c of the (n-1)st power term. Product homogeneous Monge-Ampere omits those terms. A primitive of the raw Monge-Ampere one-form near zero forces closedness. A Gauduchon three-torus has a smooth nonstationary Perron translation, and Gauduchon surfaces still have the first-derivative terms. These obstructions are settled. The curve polar metric and the positive-lower-volume complete model topology are known, as are specified product extensions. No proposed replacement action, metric or proof is supplied.
completionCriteria: Specify and prove a new coherent metric/action construction whose interpolation, stationarity and complete singularity topology fit the stated Perron/Legendre geometry on a nontrivial Hermitian domain. State whether points are potentials, ordinary models, ordinary types or test curves/rays, and justify the projection and endpoint limits. A scoped sufficient-condition theorem must have substantive genuinely nonclosed examples beyond simply constant paths or the known curve/product geometry. Do not import a Kahler energy primitive, drop torsion terms from variation, or repeat the settled raw-action obstruction as the remaining solution. Independently reconstruct the full proof with exact primary hypotheses and preserve the unresolved connection to the full P01/P17 topology programme.
